payload.summary: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh health_3001 check uses curl --max-time 3, but frontend-1's baseline response time is ~2.0-2.2s with observed spikes to 3.4s -- the timeout margin is too tight and produces recurring false FAILURE verdicts under normal jitter, not real outages.
payload.evidence: Tier-1 system-auditor investigation 2026-07-12T03:44Z: 15 sequential requests to http://localhost:3001/ measured 2.0-3.4s response time (network delay <1ms, all server-side), container 0 restarts, CPU 0%, mem 18%, stable 6h post-reboot. 3 recurring transient CURL_ERR->200-on-retry blips this session (~03:11Z, 03:15Z, 03:43Z) all traced to this same margin issue.
payload.suggested_fix: Bump curl --max-time in the health_3001 check (and likely health_3000/other HTTP checks in the same script) from 3s to something with real margin, e.g. 6-8s, in scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh. Small, low-risk, single-file change.
payload.secondary_finding_not_actionable_here: pdf-extractor showing real stress during this probe (CPU 202%, mem 92%, event-loop appeared wedged 0/3 multi-probe) but auditor assessed as expected-under-active-extraction-load, not a new regression -- pdf-extractor has been pre-existing-unhealthy since before the 2026-07-11 incident per prior session notes. Flagging for awareness only, not requesting action.
